growth_012:n1.prompt:
You are helping me build the initial target contact list for an outbound sales sequence inside {{vendor}}, our CRM. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (use your configured credentials), (2) the ideal customer profile — target industries, company sizes, job titles/roles, and any geographic or firmographic filters, and (3) a source list or criteria for sourcing prospects (e.g., a CSV I provide, or search/filter criteria to run inside {{vendor}} or a connected enrichment source).

Once you have this, please:
1. Use {{vendor}}'s API or dashboard to create the target contact records (name, title, company, email, and any other required fields) that match the ICP.
2. Link each contact to its parent company record, ensuring firmographic and contact data is auto-enriched where {{vendor}} supports it.
3. Add any custom fields needed to track sequence status or lead source.
4. Run duplicate detection and merge any duplicate contacts or companies without losing existing data.
5. Build a filtered, sorted view of this list (e.g., "Outbound Sequence Q_ Target List") and make it shared/visible for the team if that's supported.

Done looks like: a clean, deduplicated list of target contacts in {{vendor}}, each linked to an enriched company record, tagged or filtered into a dedicated view ready to be loaded into a sequence, with no missing required fields (name, email, company, title).

Report back with: the number of contacts created, the name/link of the saved view, a summary of the ICP filters used, and any duplicates merged or data-quality issues you encountered.

growth_012:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft outbound sales sequence copy inside {{vendor}}, our CRM. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in {{vendor}}: our ideal customer profile / target persona description, the core value proposition or pitch angle, any proof points (case studies, metrics, customer names we can reference), our sender name/role, and the desired sequence length (e.g., number of touches and cadence, such as 4-5 emails over 2 weeks, optionally with a call or LinkedIn step).

Once you have this context, do the following:
1. Use {{vendor}}'s built-in AI assistant to generate a first draft of the sequence, including a subject line and body for each step, tailored to the persona and value proposition I gave you.
2. Ask the AI assistant for insights/suggestions on messaging angles, subject line variants, and optimal send-day spacing based on any patterns or data available inside {{vendor}}.
3. Refine the draft so each step has a clear single call-to-action, escalating urgency across the sequence, and personalization tokens (first name, company, etc.) wherever {{vendor}} supports merge fields.
4. Save the drafted sequence as a template or sequence object inside {{vendor}}, ready to be attached to a target list, but do not activate/launch it or enroll any prospects yet.

Done looks like: a complete multi-step sequence saved in {{vendor}} with subject lines, body copy, merge fields, and timing/cadence between steps, reviewed for tone and clarity, but left in draft/inactive status.

Report back to me with: the sequence name/location in {{vendor}}, a summary of each step (subject + short description of content and cadence), any AI-suggested alternatives you considered, and a note confirming the sequence is drafted but not yet launched, pending my review.

growth_012:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up and launch an outbound sales sequence in {{vendor}}, our CRM. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already configured: my {{vendor}} instance/API access details (confirm you can use my already-configured credentials), the target list or segment criteria (or confirm it's already built in the CRM), the sequence goal (e.g., book a meeting), number of steps and cadence (e.g., 4 touches over 10 days), the email copy/talking points I want used (or draft them yourself for my review), sender identity, and any triggers I want automated (e.g., auto-create a task when a prospect replies, auto-remove from sequence on reply/meeting booked, auto-notify me on open or click).

Then do the following: (1) Draft the multi-step email sequence copy (subject lines + body for each touch) tailored to the target list. (2) Prepare the sequence configuration in {{vendor}} — steps, delays, send windows — using the documented API or dashboard, but do NOT activate or enroll any prospects yet. (3) Define the trigger-based workflow rules (e.g., reply detected → create follow-up task and pause sequence; meeting booked → notify me; no response after final step → mark as cold) as draft automations, not yet live. (4) Compile a summary showing: the target list size and source, the full sequence copy, the cadence/timing, and every automation rule you configured.

Once everything is drafted and staged, stop for human sign-off — present the summary and wait for my explicit approval before activating the sequence, enrolling any prospects, or turning on any automation rules. Do not launch anything without my confirmation. Report back with the draft sequence, the proposed automations, and a clear list of what will happen once I approve.

growth_012:n4.prompt:
You are helping me launch and monitor an outbound sales sequence in {{vendor}} (our CRM), then track replies as they arrive over the coming days. This is an async step — results land over time, so you must set up monitoring and poll for updates rather than expecting an immediate outcome.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: the target contact/company list segment or view name in {{vendor}}, the sequence or campaign name I want you to launch, the sending email account (Gmail or Outlook) to confirm is connected and syncing two-way, and any reply-handling rules (e.g., what counts as a positive reply vs. auto-reply/bounce).

Then do the following:
1. Verify the sending mailbox is connected to {{vendor}} so sent emails and replies log automatically to the right contact/company records with a full activity timeline.
2. Launch the sequence for the specified list segment, confirming enrollment counts match expectations.
3. Set up a webhook subscription (or confirm one exists) in {{vendor}} for reply/activity events so you can be notified or poll for new inbound replies without manual checking.
4. On each check-in, pull the latest activity timeline for enrolled contacts, flag new replies, classify them (interested, not interested, out-of-office, bounced), and note which contacts need follow-up or handoff to book a meeting.
5. Keep a running log of sequence status: emails sent, opens/replies if visible, and any errors (bounces, disconnected mailbox, failed sends).

Done looks like: the sequence is live in {{vendor}}, the mailbox sync and webhook/reply monitoring are confirmed working, and you have a clear, current summary of reply status per contact.

Report back with: sequence name and enrollment count, confirmation of mailbox sync and webhook setup, a categorized list of replies received so far, and any contacts flagged as ready for meeting booking or requiring my attention.

growth_012:n5.prompt:
You are helping me automate meeting booking for outbound sales responders using {{vendor}}, our scheduling tool. If any of the following are missing, ask me for them first: (1) the list of responders/leads who replied positively and need a meeting booked (name, email, and any suggested time windows), (2) my {{vendor}} event-type slug and username for the meeting type to book, (3) the CRM (e.g., Salesforce or HubSpot) where bookings should sync, and (4) preferred meeting duration and buffer/reminder settings.

Once you have these, do the following using my configured {{vendor}} credentials:
1. Check live availability for my event type via the {{vendor}} API or MCP tool-calling surface.
2. For each responder, create a booking using the create_booking (mcp) tool or the equivalent create-booking API call, matching them to the earliest mutually workable slot in their detected time zone.
3. If a responder requests a new time after booking, reschedule the existing booking via the reschedule-booking API call rather than creating a duplicate.
4. Confirm each booking triggers {{vendor}}'s automated confirmation and reminder/follow-up sequence (email/SMS) to reduce no-shows.
5. Verify each new booking flows into the CRM automatically (or via the configured integration/automation) so the deal/contact record reflects the scheduled meeting.
6. If a direct booking isn't possible for a given responder (e.g., no clear time match), generate and share their personalized booking link instead so they can self-select a time from live availability.

Done looks like: every responder either has a confirmed booking synced to the CRM with reminders active, or has received a booking link. Report back a summary listing each responder, the booking status (booked/link sent/rescheduled), the meeting time, and confirmation that CRM sync succeeded, flagging any responder where booking failed so I can follow up manually.

growth_012:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for a live outbound sales qualification call (no-screen step: the live conversation itself remains a human step and cannot be run by you). Please do the prep work only.

First, ask me for anything missing: my CRM name, the prospect's name/company/contact record, our qualification framework (e.g., BANT or MEDDIC), our ideal customer profile criteria, and any known context from prior email/reply threads.

Using your configured credentials, pull the prospect's CRM record, recent sequence emails, and reply history to build a one-page call brief. The brief should include: company snapshot, likely pain points inferred from their replies, a tailored set of open-ended discovery questions covering budget, authority, need, and timeline, and 2-3 objection-handling talking points based on our typical objections. Also draft a call agenda (opening, discovery, next steps) and a post-call CRM update template with fields for qualification outcome (qualified/disqualified/nurture), notes, and next action.

Save the brief and templates as a draft note attached to the CRM contact/deal record so I can review them before the call. Do not attempt to join, transcribe, or simulate the call, and do not update the CRM's qualification status yourself — that judgment requires my live conversation.

When done, report back: the CRM record link, a summary of the brief and questions prepared, and confirm the post-call update template is ready for me to fill in. Then stop for human sign-off before any qualification status is marked in the CRM.
